title: The Man Who Couldn't Fall
text:
Morning returned to Sera's tea shop as if the world had not nearly broken around it.

The repaired door still leaned slightly to the left.

Sera hated it.

Rhen claimed it had character.

[[speaker:sera]]“Say that again and I will give your face character.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“You have used that threat before.”

[[speaker:sera]]“It remains available.”

Rhen accepted his tea with the expression of a man who considered this a normal morning.

That was when someone collapsed outside.

Not a farmer.

Not a merchant.

A martial master.

The man's robe was torn from shoulder to waist. His breathing was shallow, but the injuries were stranger than the blood.

A physician traveling through town knelt beside him.

Sera noticed the man's hands first.

Too steady.

Too knowledgeable.

The physician touched two fingers to the victim's wrist and frowned.

Rhen looked once from inside the shop.

His expression changed by almost nothing.

Sera noticed anyway.

The physician said the victim had been struck by two incompatible patterns of internal force at nearly the same instant.

Not consecutive.

Simultaneous.

[[speaker:sera]]“Two attackers?”

The physician shook his head.

“That's what the body says.”

Rhen spoke from behind her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“One.”

The physician looked up.

“Excuse me?”

[[speaker:rhen]]“One attacker.”

“You haven't examined him.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“No.”

“Then how would you know?”

Rhen lifted his cup.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Guess.”

Sera gave him a flat look.

The physician did not believe him.

Several hours later, after the injured man woke, he confirmed it.

One opponent.

One man.

Two attacks arriving as though performed by two different cultivators occupying the same body.

The physician became very still.

Then he finally introduced himself.

Luo Wen.

World Rank #10.

The Grave Physician.

Marquis of the Last Lantern.

One of the Five Marquises.

He had been following a trail of similar victims across three provinces.

Seven masters.

Every one defeated.

Every one left alive.

Not mercy.

Documentation.

Someone was measuring strong cultivators.

Luo studied the victim again.

[[speaker:luo]]“This was deliberate.”

Sera folded her arms.

[[speaker:sera]]“You think someone is testing the ranking world.”

[[speaker:luo]]“I think someone is building a list.”

Rhen looked out the window.

A faint breeze moved one loose leaf across the road.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Then eventually they'll come here.”

Sera looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Why here?”

Rhen met her eyes.

He did not answer.

That bothered her more than if he had.

title: Two Heartbeats
text:
Luo Wen stayed.

Not as a guest.

Not exactly.

He commandeered the table nearest the window, ordered hot water, and transformed Sera's tea shop into an investigation room without asking permission.

Sera disliked him immediately.

Rhen liked him immediately because Sera disliked him.

[[speaker:sera]]“Stop smiling.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I am not smiling.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Your eyes are.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Very observant.”

Luo ignored them.

The seven victims shared one strange feature.

Every injury pattern suggested an opponent capable of maintaining two independent qi states without transitioning between them.

That should have been impossible.

A cultivator could circulate aggressively.

Defensively.

For movement.

For reinforcement.

For a weapon art.

But every complete technique required the meridian network to commit.

Even the Top Ten transitioned.

Just faster than ordinary people could perceive.

Whoever did this did not.

The trail led into the hills.

Sera insisted Rhen remain at the tea shop.

[[speaker:rhen]]“All right.”

Sera stared at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“That was too easy.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Would arguing improve your confidence?”

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Then I have made the correct decision.”

She left suspicious anyway.

Near an abandoned gate, Sera and Luo found a young man in plain grey clothes.

No visible weapon.

No obvious killing intent.

He looked almost bored.

His name was Ji Wuye.

The Second Pulse.

Sera moved first.

Ji's right hand intercepted her wrist.

At the exact same instant, without any visible transition, his left palm struck toward Luo Wen.

Luo twisted aside.

His eyes narrowed.

Ji's qi shifted.

No.

One layer shifted.

The other did not.

Luo's face changed.

[[speaker:luo]]“Two circulations.”

Ji smiled.

[[speaker:ji]]“You noticed.”

The first rhythm reinforced his body.

The second gathered offensive qi through his shoulder.

Two complete internal processes.

Running independently.

Sera disappeared behind him.

Ji turned to intercept her while his other circulation continued attacking Luo without interruption.

For three breaths, the fight felt wrong.

Not faster than expected.

Not stronger than expected.

Wrong.

Like watching one body obey two different martial logics.

Ji looked at Sera.

[[speaker:ji]]“The reports undersold you, Pale Orchid.”

Silence.

Luo Wen slowly turned toward her.

Sera closed her eyes.

Ji laughed softly.

Then withdrew.

Not fleeing.

Leaving.

Because he had learned what he came to learn.

When Sera returned to the tea shop, Rhen was exactly where she had left him.

She placed both hands on his table.

[[speaker:sera]]“He knew.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Apparently.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He knew who I was.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You don't look surprised.”

Rhen considered lying.

Sera's eyes narrowed.

He reconsidered.

[[speaker:rhen]]“I am surprised you expected him not to.”

She stared at him for several seconds.

[[speaker:sera]]“I dislike you.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“That seems temporary.”

title: Seven Debts
text:
Luo Wen now knew the tea-shop owner was World Rank #7.

He handled the revelation poorly.

[[speaker:luo]]“You are the Pale Orchid.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Quietly.”

[[speaker:luo]]“You sell tea.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:luo]]“You are one of the most feared assassins of the last generation.”

[[speaker:sera]]“The tea is also good.”

Rhen nodded.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Very good.”

Sera threw a cloth at him.

Far from the village, another fight had already begun.

Han Myeong, World Rank #8.

The Furnace Saint.

Marquis of the Burning Wastes.

A body cultivator whose furnace qi had allowed him to walk through techniques that shattered fortress gates.

Across from him stood a smiling man with empty hands.

Cao Tian.

The Collector.

Han blocked a palm strike.

Nothing.

Another.

Nothing.

A third glanced off his shoulder.

Still nothing.

Cao counted.

[[speaker:cao]]“Three.”

Han advanced.

Cao struck his forearm.

[[speaker:cao]]“Four.”

Han caught him by the collar and drove him through a stone wall.

Cao emerged bleeding, still smiling.

[[speaker:cao]]“Five.”

Han stopped.

He finally felt it.

Not pain.

Residue.

Tiny fragments of force embedded inside the places where he had blocked.

Cao lifted two fingers.

[[speaker:cao]]“Due.”

Five impacts erupted simultaneously.

Not from outside.

From where Han had already accepted them.

His reinforced body buckled.

One knee touched the ground.

For most fighters, that would have ended the story.

Han looked up.

Then laughed.

[[speaker:han]]“Interesting.”

He stood.

Cao's smile faded by half a degree.

The next exchange became different.

Han stopped treating blocked attacks as harmless.

Cao stopped allowing himself to be touched.

Seven Debts accumulated.

Then eleven.

Then fourteen.

Han's furnace qi roared hotter, burning through some of the embedded force before Cao could collect it.

Cao retreated at seventeen.

Not defeated.

Not victorious.

Satisfied.

Days later, Han followed his trail to Sera's village.

He entered the tea shop and saw Luo Wen.

Then Sera.

Then Rhen.

Han looked at Rhen for a long moment.

[[speaker:han]]“Who is he?”

[[speaker:sera]]“A regular.”

Rhen raised his cup.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Hello.”

Han looked back at Sera.

[[speaker:han]]“Your regular has the posture of someone who kills people.”

[[speaker:sera]]“He says he's a healer.”

[[speaker:han]]“That did not answer me.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Welcome to my life.”

That night, Sera confronted Rhen.

Someone had exposed her identity deliberately.

Someone had gathered records on her.

Someone was drawing ranked martial artists toward the same trail.

[[speaker:sera]]“Do not interfere.”

Rhen watched her.

[[speaker:rhen]]“If that's what you want.”

She should have been relieved.

Instead she was irritated.

[[speaker:sera]]“You could at least pretend that decision was difficult.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“It was.”

[[speaker:sera]]“You answered immediately.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I think quickly.”

She hated that answer because it was probably true.

title: The Empty Scripture
text:
The abandoned compound contained no treasure.

That was worse.

It contained records.

Years of them.

Names.

Schools.

Techniques.

Preferred ranges.

Injuries.

Habits.

Weaknesses.

Sera found her own file.

It was thicker than she liked.

Luo Wen found anatomical diagrams of several ranked fighters.

Han found records of his furnace cycles.

No one spoke for a while.

Then a sword cut through the compound's outer gate.

One line.

Clean enough that the two halves remained standing before slowly sliding apart.

Arin Vale entered.

World Rank #9.

The Silver Sword Saint.

Marquise of the Silver Horizon.

She looked at Sera.

Then Han.

Then Luo Wen.

[[speaker:arin]]“Why are all of you here?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Apparently someone is collecting us.”

Arin's expression hardened.

She had followed a man who attacked three swordsmen attached to her territory.

That man stepped from the records chamber.

Ye Mo.

The Empty Scripture.

Arin drew.

Silver flashed.

Ye barely survived the first exchange.

His sleeve split.

Blood appeared across his shoulder.

Then his circulation changed.

He repeated the internal principle behind Arin's movement.

Not the technique.

Not the mastery.

The principle.

A compressed release through the hip and wrist timed to the instant the opponent committed.

Arin stopped.

[[speaker:arin]]“Don't.”

Ye smiled.

[[speaker:ye]]“Why?”

Sera moved.

Ye watched.

Han reinforced.

Ye watched.

Luo Wen struck an acupoint.

Ye watched.

Each time his circulation altered.

Borrowed fragments.

Crude.

Incomplete.

But accumulating.

A trace of Arin's timing.

A portion of Han's reinforcement.

A sliver of Sera's acceleration.

Luo understood first.

[[speaker:luo]]“Stop showing him techniques.”

Silence.

Han looked offended.

[[speaker:han]]“You want me to punch him normally?”

[[speaker:luo]]“Yes.”

Arin sheathed her sword halfway.

[[speaker:arin]]“Humiliating.”

Sera smiled.

[[speaker:sera]]“For him.”

What followed was perhaps the least elegant battle four Marquises had ever fought.

No signature arts.

No refined forms.

No famous techniques.

Just brutally efficient fundamentals.

Ye's smile vanished.

[[speaker:ye]]“Show me something worth taking.”

Arin hit him with the flat of her scabbard.

[[speaker:arin]]“No.”

He withdrew furious.

The four stood among the records.

Han finally said what all of them were thinking.

[[speaker:han]]“These people were made for us.”

Rhen, when they returned, listened to the explanation without interrupting.

Arin noticed.

[[speaker:arin]]“You are not surprised.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I am frequently unsurprised.”

[[speaker:arin]]“I already dislike him.”

Sera folded her arms.

[[speaker:sera]]“Get in line.”

title: The Man Who Built Monsters
text:
Luo Wen spent the night proving that the Three Calamities should not exist.

Ji Wuye's dual circulation should tear his meridians apart.

Cao Tian's force-retention method should progressively damage his own channels each time he stored impact.

Ye Mo's constant reconstruction should leave scar tissue throughout his internal network.

Yet all three were stable.

Not merely surviving.

Optimized.

Someone had not taught them unusual techniques.

Someone had rebuilt them around those techniques.

Rhen read Luo's notes.

Then said one name.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Wei Zhen.”

Han stopped moving.

Arin frowned.

Luo Wen looked blank.

Sera knew the name from old rankings.

Former World #5.

A Duke from the previous generation.

Wei Zhen, later called the Hollow Duke.

A cultivation architect who vanished after retiring from the Five Dukes.

Many believed him dead.

[[speaker:sera]]“He was a Duke.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“Yes.”

[[speaker:sera]]“And you know him.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I have met him.”

Sera leaned back.

[[speaker:sera]]“Of course you have.”

Arin pointed at Rhen.

[[speaker:arin]]“Why does she say that like this happens often?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Because it does.”

Rhen ignored both of them.

Wei Zhen had once argued that martial potential was wasted because every sect forced disciples into inherited systems.

He believed cultivation should be custom-built around physiology.

Not tradition.

Not lineage.

Not style.

Body first.

Then art.

That philosophy had made him brilliant.

It had also made him dangerous.

The Three Calamities were the proof of concept.

Ji Wuye: why must one body maintain one circulation?

Cao Tian: why must force take effect when it lands?

Ye Mo: why must a cultivator commit to one martial path?

Wei Zhen had spent decades turning those questions into people.

Elsewhere, the retired Duke sat beneath a dead tree.

The Three Calamities stood before him.

Ji reported Sera's condition.

Cao reported Han's adaptation.

Ye reported the four-way encounter.

Wei listened.

Then smiled.

[[speaker:wei]]“Four.”

Ji lowered his head.

[[speaker:ji]]“Yes, Master.”

Wei looked toward the eastern mountains.

[[speaker:wei]]“One remains.”

For the first time, his intent became clear.

He was not hunting the Five Marquises individually.

He was assembling them.

title: The Sixth Marquis
text:
Ji Wuye found Qin Luo beside a mountain bell.

World Rank #6.

The Silent Bell.

Marquis of the Hollow Chime.

Strongest of the Five Marquises.

Qin did not draw his weapon immediately.

He listened.

Ji attacked.

Two complete circulations surged at once.

One reinforced the legs.

One drove force through the shoulder.

Qin shifted aside before either arrived.

Ji's eyes sharpened.

Again.

Qin avoided the first strike and disrupted the second with one tap.

Not because he saw both.

Because he heard both.

Every circulation had vibration.

Every meridian shift had rhythm.

Ji possessed two.

Qin simply listened to both at once.

For the first time since the fighting began, Ji Wuye looked excited.

[[speaker:ji]]“You can hear them.”

Qin's expression remained calm.

[[speaker:qin]]“You're loud.”

Ji attacked harder.

The duel escalated.

Qin adjusted to the first pulse.

Ji changed the second.

Qin found the new resonance.

Ji deliberately desynchronized them.

For half a breath, Qin lost the pattern.

Blood appeared at his lip.

He smiled.

[[speaker:qin]]“So that's why he made you.”

Ji stopped.

[[speaker:ji]]“You know Master?”

[[speaker:qin]]“No.”

Qin raised Wuyin.

[[speaker:qin]]“But I know what he's trying to prove.”

Their next exchange shook dust from the bell tower.

Then a voice spoke from somewhere beyond the courtyard.

[[speaker:wei]]“Excellent.”

Ji stopped instantly.

No hesitation.

No pride.

A fighter capable of forcing blood from World #6 obeyed that voice like a student called from training.

Qin's eyes narrowed.

Wei Zhen never appeared.

He did not need to.

Ji withdrew.

Qin followed the trail.

It led toward Sera's region.

By evening, Sera's tea shop contained four Marquises and one irritated owner.

Then Qin entered.

He saw Arin first.

Something passed between them too quickly for Han to notice.

Sera noticed.

Rhen noticed much earlier.

[[speaker:sera]]“Do not start.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I have said nothing.”

[[speaker:sera]]“Your face has.”

Qin looked at Rhen.

No recognition.

But a pause.

A small one.

He heard Rhen's pulse through the floor.

Too clean.

Too controlled.

Perfect.

Qin frowned.

[[speaker:qin]]“Who is he?”

Everyone answered at once.

[[speaker:sera]]“A problem.”

[[speaker:han]]“A healer.”

[[speaker:arin]]“Annoying.”

[[speaker:luo]]“Suspicious.”

Rhen lifted his cup.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Regular.”

Qin looked around.

[[speaker:qin]]“I regret asking.”

title: Five Marquises
text:
For the first time, all five Marquises stood in the same room.

Not because someone summoned them.

Not because the ranking council wanted a dramatic meeting.

Because one investigation had slowly pulled each of them toward the same enemy.

#6 Qin Luo.

#7 Sera.

#8 Han Myeong.

#9 Arin Vale.

#10 Luo Wen.

Five of the strongest living martial artists below the Dukes.

And Rhen was trying to eat breakfast.

Sera spread Wei Zhen's records across the central table.

The Three Calamities had not been sent to kill them.

They had been sent to learn.

The conclusion was obvious.

[[speaker:qin]]“He wants all five of us.”

[[speaker:han]]“Then we go to him.”

[[speaker:luo]]“That is usually how traps work.”

[[speaker:han]]“Good. Saves time.”

Arin looked at Sera.

[[speaker:arin]]“Does he always think like that?”

[[speaker:sera]]“Apparently.”

Rhen reached for another dumpling.

Sera slapped his hand away.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Cruel.”

[[speaker:sera]]“This is serious.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I know.”

The cups trembled.

All five Marquises became still.

Pressure rolled across the town.

Not killing intent.

Not an attack.

A declaration.

Wei Zhen was nearby.

The Five stood.

Rhen stood too.

Sera looked at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“No.”

Rhen stopped.

[[speaker:sera]]“You promised.”

[[speaker:rhen]]“I remember.”

[[speaker:sera]]“This is our fight.”

A pause.

Then he sat again.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Come back.”

Sera turned toward the door.

[[speaker:sera]]“Keep my tea warm.”

Rhen smiled.

[[speaker:rhen]]“Always.”

The Five followed the pressure to an abandoned mountain estate.

The Three Calamities waited in the courtyard.

Behind them sat an older man drinking tea.

Plain robes.

Grey hair.

No visible weapon.

No aura.

That absence was more frightening than pressure.

Wei Zhen looked at the Five Marquises.

Then smiled.

[[speaker:wei]]“The entire Marquis tier.”

He set down his cup.

[[speaker:wei]]“Good.”

Sera's eyes narrowed.

The retired Duke looked at her longer than the others.

Not because she was strongest.

Because something about her circulation interested him.

The same circulation Rhen had repaired years ago.

Wei's smile deepened.

[[speaker:wei]]“Let us see what this generation is worth.”

title: The Three Calamities
text:
Wei Zhen did not move.

The Three Calamities did.

Ji Wuye faced Qin Luo.

Cao Tian stepped toward Han Myeong and Luo Wen.

Ye Mo smiled at Sera and Arin Vale.

Three battles erupted.

Qin versus Ji became rhythm against rhythm.

Qin could hear both circulations.

Ji could change both independently.

Every time Qin solved one relationship, Ji rewrote it.

For the first time, the Second Pulse faced someone who could genuinely understand what he was doing.

Across the courtyard, Cao Tian began counting again.

[[speaker:cao]]“One.”

Han blocked.

Luo immediately shouted:

[[speaker:luo]]“Right forearm.”

Cao struck the wall.

[[speaker:cao]]“Two.”

[[speaker:luo]]“Wall.”

A footstep.

[[speaker:cao]]“Three.”

[[speaker:luo]]“Floor.”

Han grinned.

They had learned.

Instead of avoiding Cao's Debts, they began mapping them.

Han forced Cao backward through his own accumulated field while Luo tracked every planted impact.

Cao's battlefield slowly became a prison of his own making.

Against Sera and Arin, Ye Mo waited.

Neither woman used a named technique.

Ye's expression soured.

Sera attacked with a plain knife.

Arin used basic sword cuts.

No signature movement.

No refined circulation.

Nothing worth stealing.

[[speaker:ye]]“Show me something.”

Arin struck his wrist.

[[speaker:arin]]“No.”

Ye reconstructed a fragment of Han's reinforcement from the earlier encounter.

Sera immediately recognized the flaw.

He borrowed Arin's timing.

Arin knew exactly where it broke.

He borrowed Sera's acceleration.

Sera knew what his body could not replicate.

The Empty Scripture had accumulated pages.

The originals knew where every copied sentence was wrong.

One by one, the battles turned.

Ji Wuye fell last.

Not humiliated.

Not broken.

Qin stood over him bleeding from the mouth, Wuyin trembling from resonance strain.

The five Marquises were exhausted.

The Three Calamities were defeated.

Wei Zhen applauded once.

[[speaker:wei]]“Excellent.”

Sera stared at him.

[[speaker:sera]]“You never expected them to win.”

[[speaker:wei]]“No.”

He looked toward his disciples.

[[speaker:wei]]“They were the thesis.”

Then he looked at the Five.

[[speaker:wei]]“You are the examination.”

Wei Zhen stood.

The courtyard changed.

Only then did the Five Marquises understand how much pressure he had been withholding.

A retired Duke stepped onto the battlefield.

The gap between #5 and #6 stopped being a ranking statistic.

It became physical reality.

title: The Hollow Duke
text: The Five attacked together. It still was not enough. Qin disrupted Wei Zhen's circulation. Wei changed architecture mid-flow. Sera entered his blind side. He moved the blind side. Han absorbed a palm strike. The force bypassed his reinforcement and entered through structural gaps. Arin found a perfect opening. Wei had already placed it there. Luo Wen struck for a disabling point. The point was no longer carrying the circulation Luo expected. Wei Zhen had spent his life studying how martial systems were built. Against him, every famous art looked like a machine whose casing had already been removed. Still, the Five adapted. That mattered. Qin disrupted. Han pressured. Arin forced movement. Luo preserved function. Sera coordinated the openings. For seven exchanges, they pushed a Duke backward. Wei smiled. [[speaker:wei]]“Good.” Then he stopped testing them. One movement. The courtyard exploded outward. All five were thrown apart. Sera landed hard. Wei appeared before her. His attention had returned to her meridians. [[speaker:wei]]“Interesting.” Sera raised a needle. [[speaker:sera]]“Do not touch me.” Wei ignored the warning. Two fingers reached toward her wrist. Then stopped. A frozen petal rested between them. Wei Zhen froze. Sera looked toward the ridge. Rhen stood there. Her expression immediately changed. [[speaker:sera]]“You promised.” [[speaker:rhen]]“I did.” Rhen looked at Wei's hand. Then at Sera. [[speaker:rhen]]“Then he touched you.” [[speaker:sera]]“He did not.” [[speaker:rhen]]“He intended to.” [[speaker:sera]]“That is not how promises work.” [[speaker:rhen]]“We can debate contract language later.” Wei stared at Rhen. Recognition arrived slowly. Then all at once. [[speaker:wei]]“...You.” Rhen stepped from the ridge. For Qin, there should have been acceleration. Weight transfer. Vibration. A footfall. Anything. There was nothing. One moment Rhen was far away. The next he stood beside Sera. ✦ TRANSCENDED SKILL — TEN THOUSAND LI BENEATH ONE STEP Distance did not vanish through magic. Rhen simply crossed it with qinggong so refined that none of the Five Marquises could perceive the transition. Qin Luo, whose entire art depended on hearing movement through the world, heard nothing. That frightened him more than speed. Rhen gently moved Sera behind him. Wei's composure cracked. [[speaker:wei]]“I thought you were gone.” [[speaker:rhen]]“People keep saying that.” Wei's pride overcame his caution. The Hollow Duke released the art that once made armies retreat without battle. The entire mountain's qi network bent toward him. Stone split. Trees bowed. The Five Marquises struggled to remain standing. Rhen looked almost disappointed. One frozen petal formed above his palm. The scene ended before he moved it.

title: One Petal
text: Wei Zhen stood at the center of a mountain that had become part of his cultivation. Every vein of ambient qi fed him. Every fracture in the stone became another route. Every current in the estate answered the architecture he imposed. This was Duke-level martial power. Not merely stronger technique. A scale of control the Five Marquises could not reproduce. Rhen looked at it once. Then at Wei. [[speaker:rhen]]“You always did overbuild.” Wei's face tightened. [[speaker:wei]]“You mocked me then too.” [[speaker:rhen]]“You were easier to annoy then.” Sera stared. [[speaker:sera]]“You two know each other well enough to argue?” Neither answered her. Rhen raised one hand. A single frozen petal hovered above his fingers. ✦ TRANSCENDED SKILL — ONE PETAL It did not overpower Wei Zhen's mountain-wide art. That would have been easier to understand. The petal moved through one connection. Then another. Then another. Not cutting force. Cutting dependency. Every branch of Wei's cultivation architecture depended on a precise hierarchy of control. Rhen identified the hierarchy instantly. One petal touched the single relationship holding the entire system together. The mountain went quiet. Every connection Wei created collapsed simultaneously. No explosion. No contest of strength. His Duke-level technique simply stopped existing. It was only a Transcended Skill. That was the part Wei Zhen understood most clearly. The petal came to rest against Wei Zhen's chest. Rhen did not push it farther. Wei looked down. He understood. Another finger-width and he would be dead. The former Duke lowered himself to one knee. Nobody spoke. Qin Luo stared at Rhen as though his entire understanding of martial hierarchy had become unreliable. Han Myeong had stopped smiling. Arin Vale's sword remained half-drawn. Luo Wen was watching Rhen's pulse and finding nothing useful. Sera was furious for entirely different reasons. [[speaker:sera]]“You broke your promise.” Rhen turned. [[speaker:rhen]]“Technically—” [[speaker:sera]]“Do not.” He stopped. The Three Calamities survived. Ji Wuye accepted defeat quietly. Cao Tian laughed once and asked whether anyone had counted his remaining Debts. Nobody found that funny. Ye Mo stared at Rhen. Then attempted to reconstruct what he had witnessed. Nothing happened. No pattern. No principle. No readable circulation. For the first time, the Empty Scripture had seen a technique he could not even begin to copy. His face went pale. Wei Zhen looked at his three disciples. His life's argument had not been disproven. He had built three fighters capable of standing against Marquises. That achievement remained real. But he had been reminded of something else. There were people the ranking system could not measure. And one of them had spent years quietly drinking tea. Later, the Five Marquises returned to Sera's shop. Nobody looked at Rhen the same way. No current Duke appeared. No council assembled. No one explained the frozen-petal legend aloud. Not yet. The wider world would hear rumors later. For now, the shop closed. Sera set a cup in front of Rhen. Hard. [[speaker:rhen]]“Thank you.” [[speaker:sera]]“Who are you?” Rhen looked at the tea. Normally he would joke. Normally he would evade. Normally he would answer with something technically true. Sera sat opposite him. [[speaker:sera]]“No.” He looked up. [[speaker:sera]]“Not this time.” Long silence. Outside, one frozen petal drifted past the window. Cut to black. The night ended with one frozen petal dissolving above the roof.
